item.title: US energy chief urges IEA to abandon climate work at Paris meeting
item.description:
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright urged the International Energy Agency to abandon its work on climate change at the organization's ministerial meeting in Paris on Wednesday, intensifying a standoff that could see America withdraw from the influential global energy body.

"I want to get the support of all the nations in this noble organisation to work with us, to push the IEA to drop the climate. That's political stuff," Wright said at the biennial gathering of energy ministers from more than 40 governments.

item.title: Iran builds 'concrete sarcophagus' over nuclear site amid US talks
item.description:
Satellite imagery shows Iran is actively reinforcing its most sensitive nuclear and military installations, erecting what analysts describe as a "concrete sarcophagus" at one facility and burying tunnel entrances at another, as tensions with the United States escalate amid ongoing nuclear negotiations.

At the Parchin military complex southeast of Tehran, construction of a concrete shield over a new facility called Taleghan 2 has been completed and covered with soil, according to analysis by the Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS) reviewed by Reuters. The site has historical ties to Iran's past nuclear weapons development program and may now house a high-explosives containment chamber essential for nuclear weapon testing, though Iranian officials maintain the country is not pursuing atomic weapons.

item.title: Microsoft unveils glass storage system lasting 10,000 years
item.description:
Microsoft researchers have published a study demonstrating a data storage system capable of preserving digital information for at least 10,000 years, potentially solving a looming crisis in long-term data archiving. The findings, published in the journal Nature on February 18, represent the first successful demonstration of reliable glass storage technology for writing, reading, and decoding information at scale.

The research builds on years of work under Microsoft's Project Silica initiative, which uses powerful femtosecond lasers to encode three-dimensional pixels called voxels into glass plates roughly the size of a drink coaster. A single 12-centimeter-wide, 2-millimeter-thick square of glass can store 4.8 terabytes of data—the equivalent of around two million printed books or 5,000 films in 4K resolution.

item.title: Zelenskyy says US to monitor Ukraine ceasefire after Geneva talks
item.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced on Wednesday that negotiators have agreed on American participation in monitoring a potential ceasefire, marking a breakthrough in military discussions even as two days of U.S.-brokered peace talks in Geneva ended with diminished hopes for a broader resolution to the nearly four-year war.

Speaking to journalists after being briefed by his delegation, Zelenskyy said all three parties—Ukraine, Russia, and the United States—were "constructive on the military component" of the negotiations. "They have, in principle, agreed on almost everything there. Monitoring will definitely involve the American side. I consider this a constructive signal," Zelenskyy said, according to Ukrainska Pravda.

item.title: US sends 50 fighter jets to Middle East as Iran talks continue
item.description:
President Donald Trump has ordered a massive U.S. military buildup in the Middle East as nuclear negotiations with Iran inch forward, creating a dual-track strategy of diplomacy backed by unprecedented firepower in the region.

The USS Gerald R. Ford, the world's largest aircraft carrier, is now sailing through the Mediterranean after passing through the Strait of Gibraltar on Tuesday, according to U.S. Navy officials. The carrier is expected to reach strike range of Iran by February 20, where it will join the USS Abraham Lincoln strike group already operating in the Arabian Sea approximately 150 miles off the coast of Oman.

item.title: Russian minister says foreign spies can read soldiers' Telegram
item.description:
Russia's digital development minister on Wednesday acknowledged that foreign intelligence services can monitor messages sent by Russian troops fighting in Ukraine through the Telegram messaging app, a striking admission that comes as Moscow intensifies its crackdown on the popular platform.

Maksud Shadayev said foreign intelligence agencies "are able to see messages" sent by Russian soldiers via Telegram, the Interfax news agency reported, according to Reuters. The statement provides an unusual official justification for Russia's escalating restrictions on the messaging service, which has become deeply embedded in the country's military operations.

item.title: Macron calls social media's free speech defense 'pure bullshit'
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron sharply condemned social media platforms' free speech arguments during a visit to New Delhi on Wednesday, calling them "pure bullshit" in remarks that directly challenge a central foreign policy aim of President Donald Trump.

Speaking at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Macron argued that true free expression cannot exist when users are unaware of how opaque algorithms guide them toward content, including hate speech. "Some claim to be in favor of free speech — we are in favor of free algorithms — totally transparent," Macron said, according to Bloomberg. He added: "Free speech is pure bullshit if nobody knows how you are guided through this so-called free speech — especially when it is to be guided from one hate speech to another."

item.title: Apple plans daily product announcements leading to March 4 event
item.description:
Apple is planning to unveil a series of new devices through daily press releases during the first week of March, according to reports from Bloomberg and prominent Apple analyst John Gruber, culminating in a hands-on "special Apple Experience" event on Wednesday, March 4.

The tech giant is expected to announce the iPhone 17e on Monday, March 2, followed by updated iPads on Tuesday, March 3, and new MacBooks on Wednesday, March 4, according to Gruber of Daring Fireball. Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman confirmed that this staggered rollout is "exactly" what he is expecting based on his sources.

item.title: Microsoft warns US tech firms to 'worry' about Chinese AI subsidies
item.description:
Microsoft President Brad Smith is urging American technology companies to pay close attention to government subsidies fueling Chinese competitors in the global artificial intelligence race.

Speaking at the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi on Wednesday, Smith warned that US firms should "worry a little bit" about the financial backing Beijing is providing to its AI companies, according to CNBC. While acknowledging that the United States maintains "an advantage in terms of access to the most powerful chips in the world" and other technological innovations, Smith cautioned that Chinese government subsidies pose a mounting competitive challenge.

item.title: Scientists propose ultrastable laser in moon crater for timing
item.description:
A team of researchers from JILA, NASA, and Germany's national metrology institute has outlined a plan to deploy an ultrastable laser system within one of the Moon's perpetually dark craters, arguing the device could serve as a cornerstone for lunar timekeeping and help spacecraft land with greater precision.

The proposal, detailed in a paper posted to the arXiv preprint server this month, takes advantage of the extreme conditions found in the Moon's permanently shadowed regions, which are among the coldest environments in the solar system. Lead author Jun Ye of JILA in Boulder, Colorado, and his colleagues suggest that temperatures ranging from 20 to 50 kelvin, combined with the Moon's natural lack of vibrations and near-vacuum atmosphere, make these craters ideal hosts for a laser system that would outperform anything on Earth.

"The whole environment is stable, that's the key," Ye told New Scientist. "Even when you go through summers and winters on the moon, the temperature is still between 20 and 50 kelvin. That's an incredibly stable environment."

item.title: Colossal's resurrected dire wolves now hunt as a pack
item.description: Scientists and visitors peering through one-way glass at Colossal Biosciences' newly opened Dallas headquarters can watch as researchers work to resurrect species that vanished thousands of years ago. The self-described "de-extinction company" has unveiled its purpose-built global headquarters in Texas, a facility designed to showcase its work bringing back lost creatures like the woolly mammoth and dire wolf.

item.title: Study shows fire-prone weather days nearly tripled globally in 45 years
item.description:
The number of days when hot, dry, and windy weather creates ideal conditions for extreme wildfires has nearly tripled worldwide over the past 45 years, with researchers concluding that human-caused climate change drives more than half of this increase.

A study published Wednesday in Science Advances found that from 1979 through 1993, the world averaged about 22 "synchronous fire weather" days annually—periods when multiple regions simultaneously face conditions ripe for dangerous blazes. By 2023 and 2024, that figure had surged to more than 60 days per year.

item.title: Indonesia to deploy 8000 troops for Gaza peace mission by June
item.description:
Indonesia has announced that up to 8,000 soldiers will be prepared for deployment to Gaza by the end of June as part of the UN-authorized International Stabilization Force, marking the first firm commitment of military personnel to the multinational peacekeeping effort in the war-torn enclave.

Indonesian Army spokesperson Brigadier General Donny Pramono told the Associated Press on Sunday that the military has finalized its proposed troop structure and timeline, with an advance team of approximately 1,000 personnel expected to be ready for deployment as early as April. The decision comes as Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto arrived in Washington on Tuesday ahead of the inaugural Board of Peace summit scheduled for February 19.

item.title: Meta deal and India partnerships drive Nvidia-led market rally
item.description:
Nvidia propelled U.S. and Indian stock markets higher on Wednesday, as fresh partnerships in artificial intelligence infrastructure lifted major indexes and ignited rallies across technology and semiconductor stocks.

The S&P 500 rose 0.6% while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.8%, marking the third consecutive session of gains for both indexes. Nvidia's stock climbed as investor optimism mounted following a multiyear partnership announcement with Meta Platforms, which will deploy millions of the chipmaker's current and next-generation GPUs and CPUs in its AI data centers.

item.title: China fossils redated as oldest Homo erectus in East Asia
item.description:
Crushed skulls unearthed in central China decades ago are now confirmed to be the oldest Homo erectus remains ever found in situ in eastern Asia, according to new research published this week in Science Advances. The finding rewrites the timeline of early human migration from Africa to the far reaches of the continent.

Using a sophisticated dating technique applied to quartz sediments at the Yunxian site in Hubei Province, an international team of researchers determined the fossils are approximately 1.77 million years old — roughly 600,000 to 800,000 years older than previous estimates suggested.

item.title: Oil jumps 4% as Vance says Iran rejected U.S. demands in talks
item.description:
Oil prices recorded their largest single-day gain in four months on Wednesday after Vice President JD Vance said Iran refused to accept core U.S. demands in nuclear talks, and the Trump administration signaled military action remains on the table if diplomacy fails.

West Texas Intermediate crude futures settled up $2.86, or 4.59%, at $65.19 per barrel, while Brent crude gained $2.93, or 4.35%, to close at $70.35 per barrel, both benchmarks posting their highest settlements since late January. The rally marked the biggest one-day percentage increase for WTI since October 23.

item.title: Penn State researchers develop polymer capacitor for extreme heat
item.description:
Researchers at Pennsylvania State University have developed a new polymer capacitor capable of storing four times the energy of conventional models while operating at temperatures up to 482 degrees Fahrenheit, addressing a long-standing limitation in electronics for electric vehicles, data centers, and space exploration systems.

The findings, published Tuesday in Nature, describe a "polymer alloy" made from two inexpensive, commercially available plastics that self-assemble into a stable nanostructure when combined.

item.title: Study finds most people overconfident in spotting AI faces
item.description:
New research from Australian universities reveals that people's confidence in their ability to identify artificial intelligence-generated faces far exceeds their actual detection skills, leaving individuals and organizations vulnerable to deception.

The study, published this week in the British Journal of Psychology by researchers at UNSW Sydney and the Australian National University, found that even "super-recognizers"—individuals with exceptional face-recognition abilities—struggled to distinguish AI-generated faces from real ones.

item.title: Samsung shares hit record high on report of higher AI chip prices
item.description:
Samsung Electronics stock surged to an all-time high on Thursday after local media reported the South Korean tech giant is negotiating sharply higher prices for its next-generation AI memory chips, signaling a potential turnaround in its competitive battle with smaller rival SK Hynix.

The chipmaker's shares jumped as much as 5.4% to a record 190,900 won on the Korea Exchange, closing at 190,000 won as trading resumed following a three-day holiday. The rally comes amid renewed optimism for technology stocks globally, with the Nasdaq Composite rising 0.8% on Wednesday as investors returned to semiconductor and software sectors.

item.title: Nestlé to sell ice cream unit to Froneri in major overhaul
item.description:
Nestlé, the world's largest food and beverage company, announced Thursday that it will sell its remaining ice cream business to joint venture partner Froneri as part of a sweeping corporate overhaul aimed at streamlining operations around four core categories.

The Swiss giant, known for KitKat chocolate bars and Nescafé coffee, said it is in "advanced negotiations" to transfer the ice cream division, which includes brands like Häagen-Dazs, to Froneri—a joint venture Nestlé created in 2016 with private equity firm PAI Partners. Under the restructuring, the company will concentrate resources on coffee, petcare, nutrition, and food and snacks.
